sentences.text:
Kadari Pentaiah, vs The State Of Telangana, on 7 November,
2025
 The Honourable Sri Justice N.V.Shravan Kumar
 Writ Petition No.33801 of 2025
Order:

entities.text: Kadari Pentaiah, vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Somu Srinivas Reddy, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4 and Sri.Kiran Kumar Gattu, learned standing counsel for Telangana Bhoodan Yagna Board appearing for respondent No.5.
With their consent, the writ petition is being taken up for disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. This writ petition has been filed seeking the following prayer:-
"to declare the action of the Respondents that not releasing the balance compensation (ex-gratia) amount in respect of the land admeasuring Ac.3-20 Gts, in survey number 2/85, situated Ibrahimpatnam Village and Mandal, R.R District to petitioner by respondents is illegal, arbitrary and violate the Article 14 of constitution of India and besides being opposed to the principles of natural justice and direct the respondents to release the balance compensation (ex-gratia) balance amount as per fixed the amount by respondents in respect of the land admeasuring Ac.3-20 Gts, in survey number 2/85, situated Ibrahimpatnam Village and Mandal, R.R District to petitioner."
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner claims to be the owner and possessor of land admeasuring to an extent of Ac.3-20 Gts, in survey number 2/85, situated Ibrahimpatnam Village and Mandal, R.R District.

It is further submitted the petitioner's subject land was acquired for the purpose of establishment of OCTOPUS Commando Training Centre and notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was issued and the same was published in Gazette vide R.R.No.19 dated 23.05.2011.

The case of the petitioner is that the respondent No.5 paid half compensation amount i.e Rs.9,56,325/- through Cheque bearing No.025299 dated 25.03.2013, however, till date balance amount is not paid to the petitioner.

Thereafter, petitioner made a representation and requested respondent No.5 to release balance compensation (ex-gratia) amount and inspite of receiving the said representation on 25.06.2025, respondent No.5 failed to consider the same.
Aggrieved by the same, this writ petition is filed.

4. Though various grounds are raised in the writ petition, learned counsel for the petitioner restricts his prayer seeking a direction to respondent authorities to dispose the petitioner's representation dated 25.06.2025, in a time bound period.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4 and learned standing counsel appearing for respondent No.5 submits that if the petitioner's representation dated 25.06.2025 is still pending for consideration, respondent authorities may be directed to pass appropriate orders.

6. Recording the submission made by learned counsel appearing on either side and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondent No.5 to dispose the petitioner's representation dated 25.06.2025 and pass appropriate orders strictly in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of eight (08) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order and communicate the same to the petitioner.
7.
Accordingly this writ petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE N.V.SHRAVAN KUMAR Date:
